title: Researchers Return to a Forgotten Forest Experiment 30 Years Later—With “Astounding” Results
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentResearchers Return to a Forgotten Forest Experiment 30 Years Later—With “Astounding” ResultsA new look at the trees revealed an overlooked “win-win-win” scenario for forest maintenanceDNBy David Nield11:00 AM CDT on August 11, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleScientific studies are often focused on specific periods of time—a month on a new drug, five years of weather changes—but a team from the University of Melbourne in Australia returned to a dormant research project three decades after it began.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoCLEAR CUTTING: The original tree thinning carried out at the study site. Credit: Centre for Forest Tree Technology.The project was located in the mountain ash forest of Tanjil Bren, Victoria, in the southeast of the country. Originally undertaken in 1987, its aim was to investigate alternatives to clearfelling, or the practice of harvesting timber by completely clearing a forest patch, burning what’s left, and sowing new seeds in the fertile ashes.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
